children: The National Stock Exchange on Friday announced the price band for its ₹22,000 crore-plus Initial Public Offering, where it plans on selling shares between ₹1,700 - ₹1,785 apiece. SBI, Bank of Baroda, SBI Capital markets, New India Assurance, General Insurance Corporation, Stockholding Corporation of India, among others are classified as the selling shareholders in this IPO. Here's a look at the selling shareholders in detail and how much will they earn by trimming their stake in India's second-largest IPO in history.

State Bank of India (SBI), India's largest lender, is also the largest selling shareholder in the NSE IPO, according to the documents. The lender is looking to sell up to 1.6 crore shares in the IPO, and based on the upper end of the price band of ₹1,785, the stake sale will fetch them a sum of ₹2,856 crore on full subscription. The lender will also make a substantial profit on their stake sale as the weighted average cost of acquisition of those shares was only ₹0.8, as specified in the IPO documents.
Canada Pension Plan Investment Board

is set to sell a maximum of around 1.2 crore shares in the NSE IPO, which will fetch them ₹2,142 crore, based on the upper end of the price band of ₹1,785. However, it has the highest weighted average cost of acquisition for these shares at ₹324.13 apiece, but it will still fetch them a substantial profit.
Ananda Investments (Mauritius) Pte

is looking at selling up 1.1 crore equity shares in the NSE IPO and is set to make up to ₹1,965.5 crore, based on the upper end of the price band. Its weighted average cost of acquisition for these shares is ₹62.38.
MS Strategic (Mauritius) Ltd

is also looking at selling a maximum of 1.1 crore equity shares in the NSE IPO, which would fetch it around ₹1,965.5 crore, based on the upper end of the price band of ₹1,785. However, its weighted average cost of acquisition for these stocks has been set at ₹66.54.
The New India Assurance Company

would likely sell up to 1.05 crore shares in the NSE IPO, which would get it ₹1,874.25 crore, based on the upper end of the price band. The insurer is likely to make a substantial profit on its stake sale in NSE as the weighted average cost of acquisition of these shares is only ₹0.32.
SBI Capital Markets Ltd

is set to sell up to 87.8 lakh equity shares in the NSE IPO, which will enable it to fetch ₹1,567.23 crore. The profit it will make would also be substantial as the weighted average cost of acquisition per equity share is ₹0.38.
Bank of Baroda

is looking at selling 76.9 lakh equity shares in the IPO, which will fetch it up to ₹1,272.7 crore based on the upper end of the price band. The weighted average cost of acquisition per equity share for the same is also ₹0.54.
Stock Holding Corporation of India

is looking at selling up to 61.9 lakh equity shares in the IPO. At the upper end of the price band of ₹1,785, this stake sale will fetch it ₹1,104.9 crore, resulting in a substantial profit as the weighted average cost of acquisition per equity share is ₹0.46.
General Insurance Corporation of India

is set to sell up 61.9 lakh shares as well, which will tech it ₹1,104.9 crore at the upper end of the price band of ₹1,785 of the NSE IPO. Its weighted average cost of acquisition per equity share is ₹5.26.
Lastly,
United India Insurance Company Ltd.
will sell up 60 lakh equity shares in the NSE IPO, earning up to ₹1,071 crore, based on the upper end of the price band. Its weighted average cost of acquisition per equity share is ₹0.5.

title: NSE IPO: Here's how much SBI, BoB and other shareholders will make by trimming their stake
